audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 2-5 of the chart contradicted the page's own whys and the packet chart: win[2] said Shen while whys[2] describes you winning the Q-W punish, win[3] said Skill while whys[3] calls them 'your tank lane-control levels', win[4] said Skill while whys[4] calls it 'your last clean solo-kill window', win[5] said Shen while whys[5] says 'it is a coin-flip, not a stomp'.
audit.why: Shen's laning tools are a 400-range spirit-blade Q and an 18s Shadow Dash; once K'Sante has W and E he wins the levels 3-6 windows, and Shen's value returns through the global R later.
audit.corrected: Levels 3, 4-5 and 6 = K'Sante (6/10 each), First item = Skill; late rows stay Shen, matching the 47.42% win rate.

audit.why: Lvl 2-3, Lvl 6, first item and mid-late (his global) are the right four beats.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three problems. (a) The page said Spirit's Refuge blocks 'your Q3 cleave' — Riot's text blocks ATTACKS, not abilities, so your spells go through and only your Passive-marked auto is denied. (b) It said 'when it is down he can block', inverting up/down. (c) Stand United being an interruptible channel, and Ki Barrier shielding your burst, were absent entirely.
audit.why: The block-attacks-not-abilities distinction changes the whole trade pattern: you keep casting through the zone and hold the marked auto. And the channel means K'Sante is one of the few tops who can simply cancel a Shen ult with Q's pull or W's stun.
audit.corrected: W corrected to attack-blocking and to 'while it is up'; the Stand United channel cancel is now in spikes[1], spikes[3], late and report[5].
sources: kit file: shen R flags channel/shield

audit.whatIsWrong: 'R-recast' on K'Sante's ultimate and 'wasted unstoppable frames' on Path Maker were both asserted.
audit.why: Neither appears in Riot's text for K'Sante's R or W. The kit file's empty needsResearch means unknown, not confirmed.
audit.corrected: Both removed and replaced with mechanics the kit does state.

audit.whatIsWrong: Advice keyed to 'his taunt cooldown' with no number.
audit.why: Shadow Dash is 18s at rank 1 and Spirit's Refuge 16s — both long enough that a baited one is a full commit window.
audit.corrected: 18s and 16s written into whys[2], early and mid.

edits.before: With the full Q-W combo up you W a committed Shen and Q3 him into the knockup-pull — he has no dash to slip your range once his taunt is down.
edits.after: With the full Q-W combo up you W a committed Shen and Q3 him into the pull — Shadow Dash is his only exit and it is down 18s at rank 1.

edits.before: All Out converts your tank stats into a duelist profile and dashes through him; on his taunt cooldown you win the straight 1v1 and can R-recast to peel.
edits.after: All Out converts your tank stats into a duelist profile and dashes through him; on his taunt cooldown you win the 1v1, and your W stun cancels his Stand United channel.

edits.before: Shen's biggest threat isn't the duel — it's his global R shadow-dashing to a fed teammate, turning his even lane into a 2-lane swing you can't answer.
edits.after: Shen's biggest threat isn't the duel — it's his global R saving a fed teammate; the one answer is CC on him mid-channel, so hold your W stun for that cast.

edits.before: Level 1 is a wash — you only have Q and no engage, and Shen is a slow tank with just his Q empower, so you both farm. The thing to respect is his W, Spirit's Refuge: when it is down he can block your Q3 cleave and your Passive-marked autos entirely, so do not dump your combo into an active W or you mark nothing. His E taunt is his only real threat early, but its long cooldown means once he taunts and misses or trades it, you have a clean window to step up. Last-hit, stack a couple Q marks, and wait for your Level 3.
edits.after: Level 1 is a wash — you only have Q and no engage, and Shen is a slow tank with just his Q empower, so you both farm. The thing to respect is his W, Spirit's Refuge: while it is up it blocks attacks, not abilities, so your spells still land but your Passive-marked auto hits nothing — keep casting through the zone and hold the auto. His E taunt is his only real threat early, and at 18 seconds a missed or traded Shadow Dash hands you a clean window to step up. Last-hit, stack Q marks, and wait for Level 3.

edits.before: This is your lane-control peak. With the full Q-W combo you bait his E taunt, and the moment it is on cooldown you W a committed Shen, charge for the longer terrain-stun, and Q3 him for the knockup-pull — he has no dash to escape your range. Your sustained tank DPS off Passive move-speed stacks beats his trade unless his W is up to block it, so time your all-ins around his W and taunt windows. At 6 your All Out is the real spike: it sheds bulk for a duelist profile and dashes through him, and on his taunt cooldown you win that straight 1v1 outright.
edits.after: This is your lane-control peak. With the full Q-W combo you bait his E taunt, and the moment it is on cooldown you W a committed Shen, charging through his damage, then Q3 him for the pull — Shadow Dash is his only escape from your range. Your sustained tank DPS off Passive move-speed stacks beats his trade unless Spirit's Refuge (16s) is up blocking your autos, so time your all-ins around his W and taunt windows. At 6 your All Out is the real spike: it sheds bulk for a duelist profile and dashes through him, and on his taunt cooldown you win that straight 1v1 outright.

edits.before: Honest truth: the lane is even and Shen makes his money off the map, not the duel. You out-bulk and out-trade him in a pure 1v1 at most points, but his global R can shadow-dash to a fed teammate and win a fight you are not even in, swinging the game while you push an empty lane. Your armor stacking does nothing about that. Close on your earlier windows — bank a side-lane lead at first item and group with R as a peeler before his global picks the map apart, because if both of you just scale, his teamfight presence outreaches yours.
edits.after: Honest truth: the lane is even and Shen makes his money off the map, not the duel. You out-bulk and out-trade him in a pure 1v1 at most points, but his global R can shield a fed teammate and win a fight you are not even in. There is one answer: Stand United is a channel, so a Q pull or a W stun on him cancels it outright — hold one for the moment he starts casting. Close on your earlier windows — bank a side-lane lead at first item and group with R as a peeler before his global picks the map apart.

edits.before: Land Q3's knockup-pull to lock a Shen who used E taunt aggressively into a full W-stun follow-up
edits.after: Land Q3's pull on a Shen who used Shadow Dash aggressively, then W-stun him into the wall

edits.before: Land E taunt to walk you out of position and turn your own W charge into wasted unstoppable frames
edits.after: Land E taunt mid-W so your charge finishes facing nothing and you walk into his spirit blade

edits.before: Track Shen's Shadow Dash (Taunt): His engage CC. Dodge it. When it is down — Q3-R him.
edits.after: Track Shen's Shadow Dash: dodge it. When it is down — Q3-R him. Your W stun cancels Stand United.

notes: Both missingInteractions entries are now on the page. The biggest single fix here is Spirit's Refuge: the page said it blocks your Q3 cleave, but Riot's text blocks attacks only — abilities pass through, so the trade pattern is 'cast through it, hold the marked auto', the opposite of what was written. The same block also said 'when it is down he can block', which was backwards.
